meta.title: Agent Console UX Redesign
meta.purpose: Cut time-to-first-successful-run for new operators by redesigning the console around the tasks they actually perform.

blocks.text: New operators reach a working agent run slowly. The console exposes the full API surface up front, so the first session is spent decoding concepts — runs, tools, traces, evals — before any value appears. Your own funnel shows the drop-off between signup and first successful run. **The interface is organised around the platform's architecture, not the operator's task.**

We redesign the console around a small number of operator jobs — launch a run, inspect a trace, fix a failing eval — and let the API surface recede until it is needed. The design system stays the source of truth; every screen is built from tokens and documented states, including the ones teams usually skip: empty, loading, partial, and error.

items: Task-first information architecture, validated with your operators before any high-fidelity design.
A state-complete component set — empty, loading, error, first-run, and power-user for every core view.
Accessibility to WCAG 2.1 AA as a build requirement, not a later audit.

blocks.text: First successful run becomes a guided path, not a scavenger hunt.

rows: Operator interviews, task analysis, current-console audit
Task-first navigation model, first-run path, key flows
Console screens on your design system, state-complete
Figma (auto-layout, variables), documented states, a11y notes

items: Enterprise, data-dense product design is the core practice — not a side offering.
System-first delivery: output maps to your components, so it survives past the engagement.
Accessibility and edge-case rigor are built into how we work, not bolted on.
